text:
Phase 3 is built and all eleven rows are marked `✓ 2026-11-26`. I ran only the test files the rows name; they all pass.

One thing I did not check: whether this change makes a spec outside the plan's front matter false. I did not run the step 7 search of the spec folders for the files I changed.

I ran `test_regeneration.py`, `test_regeneration_declaration.py` and `test_commands_file.py` in one run. I ran `test_regeneration_run.py`, `test_code_mode.py` and `test_independent_review.py` in another (71 tests).

Deviations from the plan:
- `regeneration.py` cannot import `tempergraph.run.commands`. The loader refuses any engine import except `tempergraph.api`. The module runs commands through `ctx.run`/`ctx.resolve` instead, after setting the command as its own allow-list, a 600 s deadline and `.tempergraph/regeneration` as the output folder. Because of this, the tests build a real `CheckContext` rather than a stand-in.
- A script unit logs no `unit_entered` record. The `_entered` helper in `test_code_mode.py` now reads the unit from its gate record. `test_regeneration_run.py` asserts through `_entered` and gate order.
- Fixture runs commit in the run's own worktree `repo.worktrees/temperspec--I-1`, so `test_regeneration_run.py` reads its files there.
- In the linked-worktree test the package sits under `plugins/release-notes-tgraph`. A bare folder name that matches a registered name makes `author verify` write into the registered checkout. The repository's own declaration uses `plugins/...` paths, so this does not affect it.
- Editing a unit's summary does change the regenerated diagram and stamp. The worktree test also leaves `diagram/workflow.md` stale in the code commit, so the regeneration has a commit to make.

The findings function (`findings_of`) only gives the single finding of RGF-B4. Row 4.6 extends it.
